To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the absorption capacity of sulfur dioxide by ionic liquids and their mixtures with PEG depends on the solubility of sulfur dioxide in the system and on the strength of the interactions between sulfur dioxide and its neighborhood.

the absorption capacity of PEO, ionic liquid, and their mixtures for sulfur dioxide is correlated to the solvation free energy and to the strength of the interactions between SO2 and its neighborhood.

SO2 absorption capacity of the ionic liquid and the mixture of the ionic liquids with PEO is correlated with the strength of the interactions between SO2 and its environment, which in turn is related to the relative populations of cisoid and the transoid conformations of the anions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials for SO2 capture, which is of interest for the industry and for environmental applications.
the development of new ionic liquid-based materials for the capture of SO2, with a special focus on the role of the polymer in the absorption process.
the development of ionic liquid mixtures with polymers, which present good absorption capacity and high SO2 selectivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PEO is the best candidate for absorbing SO2 from the atmosphere.
the absorption capacity of the systems is correlated to the strength of interactions of the SO2 molecules with its environment and the diffusion of the absorbing species.
the ionic liquid [N4111][TF2N] presents a higher absorption capacity of SO 2 than PEO, but the mixture of both materials presents the highest SO2 absorption capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absorption of SO2 by the systems studied in this work is mainly driven by thermodynamics, with a slight effect of the dynamics on the absorption capacity.

the SO2 absorption capacity of PEO and [N4111][TF2N] mixtures is mainly governed by the solvation free energy, which is in turn related to the interactions of SO2 with the surrounding molecules and ions.
the absorption of SO2 by the mixtures containing PEO and [N4111][NTf2] is favored by the presence of the polymer, which is a result of the negative values of the entropy of absorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a mixture of an ionic liquid with a polymer is a promising material to capture SO2.
the ionic liquid and the mixtures with PEG have potential to be used as SO2 absorbing materials.

the ionic liquid [N4111][NTf2] and the mixture of this ionic liquid with 10 mol % PEO present a good compromise between SO2 absorption capacity and the ability of the system to regenerate the ionic liquid after the absorption process, and thus can be considered a good candidate for post-combustion CO2 capture.
